why.rules.quadronica: Owner's decisions (docs/decisions.md): the field grows with the difficulty (columns × rows 6×8, 7×10, 8×11), only the cells of a removed rectangle are refilled, the field always offers at least 3 rectangles, a rectangle scores cost × area + 0.5 × cost × (area − 4). 3.1: hard has 5 colours instead of 6 (owner: six colours on 8×11 were too mixed to play; a fresh field now offers 12 rectangles instead of 7); the test plays the medium field 7×10 with 5 colours (tiles on a phone were too small).
why.games.MG_znax_med.level_up_param: 3.9 (real play logs of two players, docs/analytics/players-2026-11.md): up 4200 → 6000. In the real logs the usual Medium game is far above 4200 and almost no game falls below it. 6000 keeps the share of real games above the threshold over the Medium target (at least 85 % for an ordinary player) and asks for a result that is not accidental. Before: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 7700 → 4200: 7–8 random rectangles of 581 points in 150 s on 7×10 (one per 20 s; was 13, one per 11 s). Novice 3 → 37 %, average 60 → 96 %, strong 100 %; games for the 5 steps (median): novice 164 → 13, average 8 → 5. Games under down (1680): novice 7 %. Real play logs agree (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md).
why.shell.b_mark_pnt_tables.111: Quadronica test (7 × 10, 5 colours, 90 s, 35 per cell, conditions unchanged, so the same table is in both sets). The current table loses the top of the scale: strong 89 with 35 % of attempts at 100, expert 99 with 88 % at 100. New marks: 25 / 50 / 80 / 93, strong players at 100 in 1.3 % of attempts.
why.znax_game_field.points_good_move_arr: Hard: 30 points per cell instead of 20 (Easy 20, Medium 25; the test reads sp_points_good_move_arr). With 20 a random find on the Hard field (8×11, mean area 19.5 cells) brought 547 points against 581 on Medium, so the average player's mean score was 9641 on Hard against 8637 on Medium (1.12 ×) for a game 30 s longer, and the novice's 3934 against 3870. With 30 a random find brings 820 points and the mean rises clearly on every step: novice 1853 / 3870 / 6426, average 4148 / 8637 / 14757 (Hard = 1.71 × Medium), strong 7279 / 14983 / 25456 (real field code, player of docs/games/quadronica.md §9: one random rectangle per 20 / 10 / 6 s, 4 / 2 / 1 mistakes, pace of a game CV 25 %). A slow Hard game, one rectangle per 16 s (1.6 × slower than the average player), still beats his typical Medium game (11 finds ≈ 9200 points). The mistake price stays −320 (0.4 of a random find).
why.MG_znax_easy.level_up_param: 3.9 (real play logs of two players, docs/analytics/players-2026-11.md): up 1400 → 3500. The model's novice (4 random rectangles in 120 s) turned out far weaker than people: in the real logs every Easy game, from the very first one, passes 1400 several times over, so it was not a threshold. 3500 is still passed by every real Easy game with a wide margin, which is left for a weaker newcomer (the model rates Easy much harder than people find it, so its pass rates are not used here). Before: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: easy — novice 60–75 % of games, average ≥ 95 %): up 1900 → 1400: 4 random rectangles of 352 points in 120 s on the 6×8 field with 4 colours (was 5–6). Novice 43 → 68 %, average 97 → 99 %, strong 100 %; the novice passes Easy in 4 games (median) instead of 6.
why.MG_znax_hard.level_up_param: up 15200 → 17500 with 30 points per cell: about 21 random rectangles in 180 s (one per 8.4 s) instead of 28 (one per 6.4 s); Medium asks for 13 in 150 s (one per 11 s). Average 6 → 26 % of games (target 20–30 %; median 167 → 37 games for the 10 steps), strong 60 → 87 % (target 75–90 %), novice 0 %. Games under down (7000): average 3 %. Sensitivity: if the search time follows the cells per rectangle (Hard 9.1, Medium 11.5) the average passes 56 %; with the game doc's player without the pace spread 10 %.
